items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: and the bass player was Johnny Lindsay.

ctx.x: Yeah, did it have a name, the trio?

Yeah, I said, I'm thinking, say, how we got the name, so when we got that, it wouldn't want to ask us for a name, so we started calling us Jump This and something like that, and, uh, so, uh, the place was named the Bar of Music. They always started calling it Chocolate, something like that, so the woman said, she didn't like that, she said, well, I'm going to put two names together, I'm going to use the Chocolate Bar of Music. So, uh, that's how we got, uh, then we stayed there and made a pretty good, you know,…

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: I had a group up there, it was two guitars, myself on guitar, and Kazma on guitar, Johnny and Lindsey on bass

ctx.x: One more question on the record. Who did the singing?

Oh yeah, the singing came about, and that came about, Alvin Morgan always could, you like to sing and scat like, looks like everybody was trying to do that, see. And Alvin could do that, so he was the one decided to say, yeah, well let me scat this, and say, let me take one on scat, you see. And I think that was supposed to be a band or solo for them, so as he did it so good, they just let it go through at that, you see. That was Alvin Morgan during the scatting, yeah. Al Morgan? Yeah, Al Morgan, yeah. His name…
Took men out of Sydney's band? Who's Sydney? Sydney Desby.
